title: Ukulele, Emmy Lucas and working toward a clarinet
summary: At about thirteen he played ukulele and was told by the strict pianist Emmy Lucas to study; he was saving for a clarinet when he was sent to Louisiana on vacation.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: So it seems like, I was going to school and everything and then I think I was about 13 -- I had a little ukele and was playing it (unintelligible) and there was a man named Emmy Lucas, he worked down through Harditch's Brewery and they sent him to school and he was a genius. He knew all the music, that's what he did and he was a pianist and he told me, he says, study, he was a dogmatic man. Don't come to my house unless you have some music and don't make no bad notes in here, go home, these kind of things, so I worked and I got -- no, what happened,

I was working to get a clarinet and my mother sent me to Louisiana on vacation and I had an accident which changed everything, because I used to be a good swimmer and good runner and I boxed and everything and was doing pretty good, but by the way, when I was about two years, or three years old, I saw my mother and the streetcar was coming up the street and I ran to meet my mother and the streetcar cut the sandal off from my ankle, so, I'll tell you about that later.
